description: From the rim, the giant terraced pit of Corta Atalaya opens below — vast concentric terraces of the old open-cast mine caught in moonlight, their ochre and rust walls stepping down into shadow. The pit's sheer scale fills the frame, a man-made canyon over a kilometer across. Once among the world's largest open-pit mines, tonight it lies silent under the moon, a monument to the Riotinto mining age.

prompts.prompt-r1.txt: Photorealistic original artistic interpretation (not a photograph) of the Corta Atalaya open-pit mine, Minas de Riotinto, Huelva, Spain, at night. Tourist viewpoint: the official Mirador de Corta Atalaya, looking into the pit. Frame: the vast terraced open-pit bowl of Corta Atalaya centered, its concentric terraces descending; rust-red, ochre and violet mineral strata banding the terraced walls; the dark still depths of the pit floor far below under a starry sky. Night light: restrained moonlight and starlight on the terraced mineral walls, no floodlighting, clear starry sky, 21 degrees C, almost no wind. Main subject centered to survive a 4:5 center crop. No identifiable people, no legible logos, no text, lettering or signs anywhere in the image. Keep the lower third clean and uncluttered.
